source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament (with some Hebrews + Pauline epistles lacunae); complete Matthew
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360)
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: No early-papyrus witness preserves Matthew 28 within the 2nd-3rd c. CE corpus; the closing chapter of Matthew is attested in the early codices Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Bezae (D, 5th c. CE) + Washingtonianus (W, 4th/5th c. CE) + Alexandrinus (A, 5th c. CE). The Great Commission baptismal formula (v.19) is also attested in the patristic citations: Didache 7 (late 1st / early 2nd c. CE) uses the trinitarian formula; Justin Martyr *1 Apol.* 61 (~155 CE) cites it; Eusebius *Demonstratio Evangelica* III.5-7 and *Historia Ecclesiastica* III.5.2 (early 4th c. CE) in numerous citations gives a SHORTER form 'in my name' — the textual-critical significance of this is documented at v.19.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017)
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus; the trinitarian-formula textual question at v.19 is specifically flagged for further philological investigation
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference + Eusebius citation-witness per Conybeare, F. C., 'The Eusebian Form of the Text of Matt. 28:19' (*ZNW* 2, 1901, 275-288) and the scholarly response-tradition (e.g., Riggenbach, Chase, Cuthbert Lattey, and modern reassessment).
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c. CE). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments (4th c. CE). Davies-Allison ICC 1988-1997 (vol 3); Luz Hermeneia 2001-2005 (vol 3); France NICNT 2007; Hagner WBC 1995; Nolland NIGTC 2005; Brown, R. E., *The Death of the Messiah* (Doubleday 1994); Wright, N. T., *The Resurrection of the Son of God* (Fortress 2003); Conybeare 1901; Hubbard, B. J., *The Matthean Redaction of a Primitive Apostolic Commissioning* (SBL 1974); Kupp, D. D., *Matthew's Emmanuel* (Cambridge 1996); Levine-Brettler JANT 2017.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra (ΙΣ, ΧΣ, ΚΣ, ΘΣ, ΠΝΑ, ΥΣ, ΠΗΡ) appear abbreviated in the uncials. The closing of Matthew is text-critically stable in the uncial tradition; the principal text-critical question is the v.19 baptismal-formula form (preserved in all Greek MSS but variably attested in Eusebius's pre-Nicene citations — see v.19 notes). The chapter concludes the Gospel with no longer-ending tradition (in contrast to Mark 16, which has multiple endings).

verses.text: Ὀψὲ δὲ σαββάτων, τῇ ἐπιφωσκούσῃ εἰς μίαν σαββάτων, ἦλθεν Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία θεωρῆσαι τὸν τάφον.
verses.translit: Opse de sabbatōn, tē epiphōskousē eis mian sabbatōn, ēlthen Maria hē Magdalēnē kai hē allē Maria theōrēsai ton taphon.
verses.notes: **RESURRECTION-NARRATIVE OPENING (vv.1-10)**. *opse sabbatōn* — temporally ambiguous: 'late on the Sabbath' or 'after the Sabbath' (the latter is the standard reading; sabbath ended at sundown Saturday). *tē epiphōskousē eis mian sabbatōn* — 'as it began to dawn toward the first (day) of the week' — *epiphōskō* is also temporally ambiguous (literal dawn-light vs Jewish-reckoning evening-twilight of a new day; cf. Luke 23:54). Most likely temporal reading: Sunday dawn. *mian sabbatōn* — Hebraistic for 'first of the week' (cf. Hebrew *ʾeḥad ha-šabbāt*). The women: Mary Magdalene + 'the other Mary' (Matthew's idiom for Mary the mother of James/Joses, cf. 27:56, 61). Note: Mark and Luke list more women; John has only Mary Magdalene. The textual divergence among the four resurrection narratives is the foundational synoptic-problem locus for resurrection-tradition reconstruction (Brown 1994 *Death of the Messiah*; Wright 2003 *Resurrection of the Son of God*). *theōrēsai* (to look at / observe) — Matthew omits the Marcan anointing-spice purpose (Mk 16:1).

verses.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας· ἄγγελος γὰρ κυρίου καταβὰς ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καὶ προσελθὼν ἀπεκύλισεν τὸν λίθον καὶ ἐκάθητο ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai idou seismos egeneto megas· angelos gar kyriou katabas ex ouranou kai proselthōn apekylisen ton lithon kai ekathēto epanō autou.
verses.notes: **MATTHEAN SONDERGUT — the earthquake and angelic descent**. Matthew alone among the synoptics narrates the stone-rolling-back as an active angelic event. *seismos megas* — paralleling the *seismos* at the crucifixion (Mt 27:51, 54 — Matthean signature). *angelos kyriou* — LXX standard idiom (cf. Mt 1:20, 24; 2:13, 19). *katabas ex ouranou* (having come down from heaven) — Matthean addition; Mark/Luke find the stone already rolled away. The angelophanic scene is more theatrical in Matthew. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: the canon-reading construes the descending-from-heaven figure as Elohim-emissary — preserve text as theophanic angel-figure, the descended-from-the-sky idiom is LXX-standard.

verses.text: ἦν δὲ ἡ εἰδέα αὐτοῦ ὡς ἀστραπὴ καὶ τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτοῦ λευκὸν ὡς χιών.
verses.translit: ēn de hē eidea autou hōs astrapē kai to endyma autou leukon hōs chiōn.
verses.notes: *eidea* (form / appearance) — variant: some witnesses read *idea* (idea); SBLGNT/NA28 prefer *eidea*. *hōs astrapē* (as lightning) — luminosity-idiom; cf. Dan 10:6 LXX (*to prosōpon autou hōsei horasis astrapēs* — the Danielic man-in-linen) — direct intertext. *leukon hōs chiōn* (white as snow) — Dan 7:9 LXX (the Ancient-of-Days *to enduma autou hōsei chiōn leukon*) — the angelic figure here is described in language Daniel applied to the Ancient-of-Days. **CROSS-CORPUS Mt 17:2** (the Transfiguration luminosity) — Matthean luminosity-typology of theophanic / angelophanic appearance. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: preserve the Danielic intertext.

verses.text: ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ φόβου αὐτοῦ ἐσείσθησαν οἱ τηροῦντες καὶ ἐγενήθησαν ὡς νεκροί.
verses.translit: apo de tou phobou autou eseisthēsan hoi tērountes kai egenēthēsan hōs nekroi.
verses.notes: **MATTHEAN SONDERGUT — the guards' incapacitation**. The guards (*hoi tērountes*, those keeping watch — set up at Mt 27:62-66, Matthean redactional material) are paralyzed. *eseisthēsan* (were shaken) — pun on the v.2 *seismos*. *egenēthēsan hōs nekroi* (became as dead) — ironic: the guardians of the corpse become corpse-like while the actual corpse is gone.

verses.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν ταῖς γυναιξίν· Μὴ φοβεῖσθε ὑμεῖς, οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον ζητεῖτε·
verses.translit: apokritheis de ho angelos eipen tais gynaixin· Mē phobeisthe hymeis, oida gar hoti Iēsoun ton estaurōmenon zēteite·
verses.notes: *Mē phobeisthe* (do not fear) — standard angelophanic-reassurance idiom (cf. Mt 1:20; 14:27; 17:7; Luke 1:13, 30; 2:10). *Iēsoun ton estaurōmenon* (Jesus the crucified) — perfect-passive participle, emphasizing the abiding crucified-status of the now-risen one (cf. 1 Cor 1:23 *Christon estaurōmenon*; 1 Cor 2:2).

verses.text: οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν· δεῦτε ἴδετε τὸν τόπον ὅπου ἔκειτο.
verses.translit: ouk estin hōde, ēgerthē gar kathōs eipen· deute idete ton topon hopou ekeito.
verses.notes: **THE RESURRECTION-ANNOUNCEMENT**. *ēgerthē* (he was raised / he is risen) — aorist passive of *egeirō*; the divine-passive resurrection-formula. The *kathōs eipen* (as he said) appeals back to the three passion-predictions (Mt 16:21; 17:23; 20:19 — the third-day-resurrection formula). *deute idete* (come, see) — invitation to evidence; the empty-tomb proof-structure. Variant: some witnesses (including Sinaiticus) add *ho kyrios* after *ekeito* (where the LORD lay); SBLGNT/NA28/Vaticanus omit.

verses.text: καὶ ταχὺ πορευθεῖσαι εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἰδοὺ προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε· ἰδοὺ εἶπον ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: kai tachy poreutheisai eipate tois mathētais autou hoti Ēgerthē apo tōn nekrōn, kai idou proagei hymas eis tēn Galilaian, ekei auton opsesthe· idou eipon hymin.
verses.notes: **THE GALILEE-INSTRUCTION**. *proagei hymas eis tēn Galilaian* (he goes before you into Galilee) — Matthean (and Marcan) signature post-resurrection-rendezvous location. **CROSS-CORPUS to Mt 26:32** (Jesus's pre-arrest prediction); **CROSS-CORPUS Mk 16:7** (verbatim parallel). The Galilee-vs-Jerusalem post-resurrection-appearance tradition is the classic synoptic divergence (Matthew + Mark = Galilee; Luke + John 20 = Jerusalem; John 21 = Galilee). *idou eipon hymin* (behold I have told you) — angelic-message-completion formula.

verses.text: καὶ ἀπελθοῦσαι ταχὺ ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου μετὰ φόβου καὶ χαρᾶς μεγάλης ἔδραμον ἀπαγγεῖλαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai apelthousai tachy apo tou mnēmeiou meta phobou kai charas megalēs edramon apangeilai tois mathētais autou.
verses.notes: *meta phobou kai charas megalēs* (with fear and great joy) — Matthean characteristic emotional-doubling. Marked contrast with Mark 16:8 (the women's silence-from-fear ending). Matthew's women obey and report; Mark's flee in silence. The Matthean redaction normalizes the disturbing Marcan ending.

verses.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ Ἰησοῦς ὑπήντησεν αὐταῖς λέγων· Χαίρετε· αἱ δὲ προσελθοῦσαι ἐκράτησαν αὐτοῦ τοὺς πόδας καὶ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai idou Iēsous hypēntēsen autais legōn· Chairete· hai de proselthousai ekratēsan autou tous podas kai prosekynēsan autō.
verses.notes: **RISEN JESUS APPEARS TO THE WOMEN — first appearance**. Matthew alone narrates this appearance (John 20:14-18 has the Mary-Magdalene-only appearance; Mark 16:1-8 has no appearances in the original ending). *Chairete* (greetings / rejoice) — standard 1st-c. Greek greeting; in context echoes the v.8 *charas*. *ekratēsan autou tous podas* (grasped his feet) — physical-tangibility detail, paralleled in Luke 24:39-43 (the eating-fish proof) and John 20:27 (the wound-touching invitation) — the apologetic anti-docetic emphasis on the bodily-resurrection. *prosekynēsan autō* — worship-prostration. Variant: some witnesses omit *hōs de eporeuonto apangeilai tois mathētais autou* at the start of v.9 (a longer Byzantine reading); SBLGNT/NA28/Vaticanus omit (shorter text).

verses.text: τότε λέγει αὐταῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ φοβεῖσθε· ὑπάγετε ἀπαγγείλατε τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς μου ἵνα ἀπέλθωσιν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, κἀκεῖ με ὄψονται.
verses.translit: tote legei autais ho Iēsous· Mē phobeisthe· hypagete apangeilate tois adelphois mou hina apelthōsin eis tēn Galilaian, kakei me opsontai.
verses.notes: Re-instruction echoing the angel's v.7 message. Note: *tois adelphois mou* (to my brothers) — Matthean usage of *adelphoi* for the disciples (cf. Mt 12:48-50; 25:40 — the cross-corpus link to the Sheep-and-Goats *tōn adelphōn mou*). The women function as apostles-to-the-apostles — the *apostolos apostolōn* tradition (later Augustinian / Aquinas designation of Mary Magdalene).

verses.text: Πορευομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἰδού τινες τῆς κουστωδίας ἐλθόντες εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀπήγγειλαν τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν ἅπαντα τὰ γενόμενα.
verses.translit: Poreuomenōn de autōn idou tines tēs koustōdias elthontes eis tēn polin apēngeilan tois archiereusin hapanta ta genomena.
verses.notes: **THE GUARDS-BRIBED PERICOPE OPENING (vv.11-15) — MATTHEAN SONDERGUT**. *koustōdia* — Latin loanword (*custodia* = guard-detail), introduced at Mt 27:65-66. The Latinism is Matthean-distinctive evidence for a Greek-speaking community with Roman administrative-vocabulary familiarity. The pericope serves an explicit Matthean apologetic-polemical function — see v.15 *para Ioudaiois mechri tēs sēmeron hēmeras*. cf. Davies-Allison ICC 3.658-664.

verses.text: καὶ συναχθέντες μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων συμβούλιόν τε λαβόντες ἀργύρια ἱκανὰ ἔδωκαν τοῖς στρατιώταις
verses.translit: kai synachthentes meta tōn presbyterōn symboulion te labontes argyria hikana edōkan tois stratiōtais
verses.notes: *symboulion* (council / plan) — Matthean term for the chief-priests-and-elders deliberations (cf. 12:14; 22:15; 27:1, 7; 28:12 — six occurrences, all Matthean signature). *argyria hikana* (sufficient silver / a substantial sum) — echo of the *triakonta argyria* (thirty pieces of silver) of Judas (Mt 26:15; 27:3-10). The silver-as-bribe-and-betrayal-motif structures Matthew's passion-resurrection narrative.

verses.text: λέγοντες· Εἴπατε ὅτι Οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς ἐλθόντες ἔκλεψαν αὐτὸν ἡμῶν κοιμωμένων·
verses.translit: legontes· Eipate hoti Hoi mathētai autou nyktos elthontes eklepsan auton hēmōn koimōmenōn·
verses.notes: **THE STOLEN-BODY HYPOTHESIS** — the earliest documented Jewish-Christian polemical exchange on the resurrection. The Matthean redactional move: by depicting Jewish authorities themselves AS the inventors of the stolen-body story, Matthew preemptively counters the contemporary (~80s-90s CE) Jewish-anti-Christian polemic. Cf. Justin Martyr *Dial.* 108 (the stolen-body charge as still circulating in 2nd-c. Jewish polemic); Tertullian *De Spectaculis* 30. The Matthean apologetic structure: the guards saw it but were paid to lie. Davies-Allison ICC 3.660-661.

verses.text: καὶ ἐὰν ἀκουσθῇ τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος, ἡμεῖς πείσομεν αὐτὸν καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀμερίμνους ποιήσομεν.
verses.translit: kai ean akousthē touto epi tou hēgemonos, hēmeis peisomen auton kai hymas amerimnous poiēsomen.
verses.notes: *ho hēgemōn* = the governor = Pilate. The detail (chief priests committing to manage Pilate on the guards' behalf) presupposes the chief-priests-Pilate cooperation already established in the trial (Mt 27:1-2, 11-26) and the guard-grant (27:62-66). *amerimnous poiēsomen* — 'we will make you free from worry' (legal-administrative protection). Possible reflection of the 1st-c. cuius regio dynamic — Roman officials accepting payments from local elites to manage perceived embarrassments.

verses.text: οἱ δὲ λαβόντες τὰ ἀργύρια ἐποίησαν ὡς ἐδιδάχθησαν. καὶ διεφημίσθη ὁ λόγος οὗτος παρὰ Ἰουδαίοις μέχρι τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
verses.translit: hoi de labontes ta argyria epoiēsan hōs edidachthēsan. kai diephēmisthē ho logos houtos para Ioudaiois mechri tēs sēmeron hēmeras.
verses.notes: **THE 'TO THIS DAY' FORMULA** — explicit Matthean redactional aside placing the polemical context in the writer's present (likely 80s-90s CE post-70-CE Jewish-Christian community-tension situation). *para Ioudaiois* — 'among the Jews' — note: this is one of the verses cited in modern reception as evidence of Matthew's distance from / opposition to formative Judaism, possibly reflecting the post-70 synagogue-vs-Jesus-movement separation. Modern scholarship contests whether 'the Jews' in Matthew is intra-community polemical (Matthew written from within Jewish communities) or extra-community polemical (Matthew written outside them). Davies-Allison ICC 3.663-664; Levine-Brettler JANT note ad loc.

verses.text: Οἱ δὲ ἕνδεκα μαθηταὶ ἐπορεύθησαν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν εἰς τὸ ὄρος οὗ ἐτάξατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς,
verses.translit: Hoi de hendeka mathētai eporeuthēsan eis tēn Galilaian eis to oros hou etaxato autois ho Iēsous,
verses.notes: **GREAT-COMMISSION PERICOPE OPENING (vv.16-20)**. *hoi hendeka* (the eleven) — the post-Judas residual disciple-group; the term *hendeka* becomes the technical designation in early-Christian usage (cf. Mt 28:16; Mk 16:14; Luke 24:9, 33; Acts 1:26; 2:14). *eis to oros* (to THE mountain) — definite article without antecedent specification; either (a) refers to a previously-specified mountain (not narrated in extant Matthew but presupposed), or (b) generic mountain-of-revelation idiom (echoing Mt 5:1 the Sermon-on-the-Mount; Mt 17:1 the Transfiguration). Matthean mountain-typology is a structural-signature device: the five major mountain-scenes shape the Gospel. cf. Davies-Allison ICC 3.679-681.

verses.text: καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν προσεκύνησαν, οἱ δὲ ἐδίστασαν.
verses.translit: kai idontes auton prosekynēsan, hoi de edistasan.
verses.notes: **MAJOR EXEGETICAL CRUX — *hoi de edistasan* ('but some doubted' / 'but they doubted')**. The Greek is grammatically ambiguous: *hoi de* can mean (a) 'but SOME (of them)' — partitive sense, or (b) 'but THEY' — referring to the same group of eleven who just worshipped. Reading (a) is the standard English-translation choice; reading (b) is grammatically defensible. *edistasan* (from *distazō*, the only other NT occurrence is Mt 14:31, of Peter on the water) — does not mean 'disbelieved' (*apistein*) but rather 'hesitated' / 'wavered' / 'was of two minds.' The interpretive issue: how can the eleven both worship AND doubt? Modern interpreters propose: (i) the eleven all wavered initially then worshipped (sequential reading); (ii) some genuinely doubted (residual unfaithfulness even at the post-resurrection appearance); (iii) the verb describes the existential-fragility of even authentic worship. Davies-Allison ICC 3.681-682; Hagner WBC 2.884-885. **NO RESOLUTION; preserve the textual ambiguity.**

verses.text: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἐδόθη μοι πᾶσα ἐξουσία ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς.
verses.translit: kai proselthōn ho Iēsous elalēsen autois legōn· Edothē moi pasa exousia en ouranō kai epi gēs.
verses.notes: **THE GREAT-COMMISSION'S AUTHORITY-CLAIM**. *Edothē moi pasa exousia* (all authority has been given to me) — divine-passive (given by the Father). **MAJOR CROSS-CORPUS to Dan 7:13-14 LXX**: *kai edothē autō exousia kai pasa basileia tou ouranou tou douleuein autō* ('and there was given to him authority and every kingdom of heaven to serve him') — the Son-of-Man enthronement passage. Matthew's *en ouranō kai epi gēs* extends the Danielic heavenly-authority to comprehensive cosmic-rule. The verbal echo to Dan 7 is unmistakable; this is the Matthean explicit Son-of-Man enthronement-claim made of the risen Jesus. **CROSS-CORPUS Mt 11:27** *panta moi paredothē hypo tou patros mou* (the prior pre-resurrection authority-claim). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: the Raëlian canon engages this verse as 'the Elohim-conferred-authority of the engineered-messenger' — preserve text + Danielic intertext; do NOT pre-resolve. Davies-Allison ICC 3.682-683.

verses.text: πορευθέντες οὖν μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος,
verses.translit: poreuthentes oun mathēteusate panta ta ethnē, baptizontes autous eis to onoma tou patros kai tou huiou kai tou hagiou pneumatos,
verses.notes: **THE GREAT-COMMISSION CORE + THE TRINITARIAN BAPTISMAL FORMULA. HIGHEST TEXT-CRITICAL CRUX OF THE CHAPTER.** The verse contains two structural components: (a) the imperative-clause *mathēteusate panta ta ethnē* (make disciples of all the nations) — note the verb is *mathēteuō* (disciple) with two participial modifications (*baptizontes* and *didaskontes* v.20); (b) the *eis to onoma tou patros kai tou huiou kai tou hagiou pneumatos* baptismal formula. **MAJOR TEXT-CRITICAL QUESTION — THE TRINITARIAN-FORMULA HYPOTHESIS**: ALL extant Greek MSS (every single one, including Vaticanus, Sinaiticus, Bezae, Washingtonianus, all uncials, all minuscules, all known versions) preserve the trinitarian-formula reading. The text-critical question arises not from any extant manuscript variant but from the citation-pattern of Eusebius of Caesarea (c. 260-340 CE). Eusebius cites the verse 17+ times in his pre-Nicene works (notably *Demonstratio Evangelica* III.5-7; *Historia Ecclesiastica* III.5.2; *Theophany* IV.16) with a SHORTER form: *poreuthentes mathēteusate panta ta ethnē en tō onomati mou* ('go and make disciples of all the nations in my name'), omitting the trinitarian-formula. After the Council of Nicaea (325 CE), Eusebius's citations shift to the full trinitarian form. Conybeare (*ZNW* 1901) proposed that the shorter Eusebian form was the original Matthean reading, and the trinitarian formula a later (early-2nd-c.) liturgical-insertion that quickly became universal. This hypothesis has been debated for over a century: arguments AGAINST Conybeare's reconstruction include (i) the trinitarian formula is already present in Didache 7 (late 1st / early 2nd c. CE — virtually contemporaneous with Matthew); (ii) Justin Martyr (*1 Apol.* 61, ~155 CE) attests the trinitarian form; (iii) Eusebius's shorter form may be paraphrastic-summary rather than verbatim-citation; (iv) NO Greek manuscript supports the shorter reading. Arguments FOR Conybeare include (i) the consistency of Eusebius's pre-Nicene citations; (ii) the early-Christian baptismal liturgy elsewhere attests baptism 'in the name of Jesus' (Acts 2:38; 8:16; 10:48; 19:5) rather than trinitarian; (iii) the developed Trinitarian theology is generally regarded as post-1st-c. **Modern scholarship is divided. NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT/THGNT all print the trinitarian formula without bracketing — the manuscript-evidence is unambiguous in supporting it**. The Conybeare hypothesis is a citation-based historical-reconstruction proposal, not a text-critical variant in the documentary-evidence sense. **LENS-RISK FLAG for the Editor**: PRESERVE the canonical text (the trinitarian formula) per the Greek manuscript tradition; DOCUMENT the Eusebian-citation-anomaly + Conybeare-hypothesis + the early Didache/Justin attestation as one position in modern philological scholarship; do NOT pre-resolve toward either (a) the orthodox-Trinitarian original-text position or (b) the Conybeare/liturgical-insertion hypothesis. **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE — INDIRECT**: the canon's general posture on Trinitarian theology (Raël reads 'Father, Son, Holy Spirit' as Elohim-civilization, engineered-messenger, transmission-medium / communication-modality) attaches to this verse. *panta ta ethnē* — 'all the nations'; the universalist-mission climax of Matthew, in apparent tension with Mt 10:5-6, 15:24 (mission-restricted-to-Israel-only); the standard reading: post-resurrection expansion of the prior Israel-only mission to all peoples. cf. Davies-Allison ICC 3.682-684; Luz Hermeneia 3.628-632; Hubbard 1974 (the redactional-history monograph); Kupp 1996.

verses.text: διδάσκοντες αὐτοὺς τηρεῖν πάντα ὅσα ἐνετειλάμην ὑμῖν· καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰμι πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας ἕως τῆς συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος.
verses.translit: didaskontes autous tērein panta hosa eneteilamēn hymin· kai idou egō meth' hymōn eimi pasas tas hēmeras heōs tēs synteleias tou aiōnos.
verses.notes: **THE EMMANUEL FRAME-INCLUSIO — THE GOSPEL'S CLOSING WORDS**. The teaching-content of discipleship: *tērein panta hosa eneteilamēn hymin* — keeping everything commanded (cf. Mt 5-7 Sermon on the Mount; Mt 10 Mission Discourse; Mt 13 Parables; Mt 18 Community Discourse; Mt 24-25 Olivet — the five Matthean teaching-blocks). *idou egō meth' hymōn eimi* — 'behold I am with you' — **MAJOR CROSS-CORPUS FRAME-INCLUSIO to Mt 1:23**: *Emmanouēl ho estin methermēneuomenon Meth' hēmōn ho theos* ('Emmanuel, which is translated, God with us'). The Matthean Gospel opens with the Emmanuel-naming and closes with the Emmanuel-promise; this is one of the most elegant structural inclusios in NT literature (Kupp 1996 *Matthew's Emmanuel* monograph entire on this device). *pasas tas hēmeras* (all the days) — comprehensive temporal claim. *heōs tēs synteleias tou aiōnos* (until the consummation of the age) — Matthean signature phrase (cf. 13:39, 40, 49; 24:3; 28:20 — five occurrences). The phrase forms an Olivet-Discourse-inclusio (24:3 the disciples' question *kai ti to sēmeion tēs sēs parousias kai synteleias tou aiōnos* → 28:20 Jesus's answer). **NO OUTRIGHT POST-RESURRECTION ASCENSION NARRATIVE** in Matthew — the Gospel closes with Jesus still on the mountain with the eleven; the *meth' hymōn* presence is left open as ongoing, in contrast to Luke 24:50-51 / Acts 1:9-11 (the explicit ascension). The structural choice is deliberate: Matthew ends with the Emmanuel-presence-unending. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: the canon reading construes *meth' hymōn eimi* as 'I (the engineered-messenger / the Elohim-emissary) remain with you in technologically-mediated communication' — preserve text + Mt 1:23 frame-inclusio; do NOT pre-resolve. **GOSPEL CONCLUSION — NO FURTHER VERSES.** Davies-Allison ICC 3.687-689; France NICNT 1118-1120; Kupp 1996 200-238.
